sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are writing from the CHD2-related epileptic encephalopathy community to your SCN1A-related seizure disorders community because public records show that both conditions have a confirmed gene-disease link and are recorded on the same broad mechanism road of too little protein from loss of function.

Public records also show high phenotype similarity between the two conditions, with overlap in atonic seizures, generalized myoclonic seizures, tonic seizures, febrile seizures between 3 months and 6 years, and seizures brought on by febrile infection.
We know that similarity does not make the conditions the same, but it does suggest that some of your community's experience may help ours.
Gene2Phenotype lists a definitive gene link for CHD2-related epileptic encephalopathy and for SCN1A-related seizure disorders.
Gene2Phenotype also records loss of function, inferred from variant types, for both conditions.
Public records show that both communities have patient organizations, including Coalition to Cure CHD2 and the Dravet Syndrome Foundation.

Public records show registry or natural history activity for both communities, including the CHD2 Natural History Project and SCN1A studies NCT06504511 and NCT06967727, and both also appear in Simons Searchlight.
Published studies report disease models for both genes, with 17 PubMed records noted for CHD2 and 257 for SCN1A.
Public records show active NIH-funded research in both areas in FY2025-2026, with 4 CHD2 projects and 8 SCN1A projects listed.

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: Public records suggest that registry design and natural history protocols may be useful to adapt from your community to ours, especially from NCT06504511, NCT06967727, and Simons Searchlight, but age of onset and severity still need review before anything is adopted.
Public records also suggest that outcome measures and endpoints may overlap enough to review for reuse, with the same caution about age of onset and severity.

Public records suggest that your clinical network, sites, and investigators may point us toward clinicians who see a similar clinical picture, including through Simons Searchlight, the Dravet Syndrome Foundation, and SCN1A studies such as NCT07531745, NCT06872125, NCT05419492, and NCT06283212.

We would also value learning how your community organized around multiple SCN1A-targeted trials, because a ClinicalTrials.gov record states that SCN1A has gene-level trials including antisense and gene therapy, while we found no public record of a targeted CHD2 clinical trial.
We found no public record of a targeted clinical trial for CHD2, while public records show 7 gene-level SCN1A trials with the highest phase listed as phase 3.

We also found no public record of an approved disease-specific therapy for CHD2, while FDA records named in public sources list cannabidiol, fenfluramine, and stiripentol for Dravet syndrome, with indication text that names Dravet syndrome specifically.
We must not assume that SCN1A disease models transfer directly to CHD2, because published model systems are gene-specific even when the broader mechanism road is similar.

We also must not assume that a targeted SCN1A treatment approach will fit every CHD2 family, because mechanism is recorded per gene and disease, not per family, and a clinical geneticist needs to confirm whether a child's own variant acts through loss of function, gain of function, or a dominant negative effect.
Public records further note that the recorded mechanisms for both CHD2 and SCN1A are inferred from variant types rather than direct functional studies.
We also cannot assume that any CHD2 family would be eligible for an SCN1A trial, and a ClinicalTrials.gov record states that one SCN1A study excludes gain-of-function variants.

Public records also note that the listing for the Dravet Syndrome Foundation was auto-checked and not human verified, so we would want to confirm the right contact and whether your community runs a registry before relying on that listing.
Do the age of onset and typical severity of SCN1A-related disease match ours closely enough for your registry items and outcome measures to apply.
Is the Dravet Syndrome Foundation the right contact, and does your community run a registry.
Has a child's specific CHD2 variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition.
What functional evidence exists for CHD2, given that the recorded mechanism is inferred from variant types rather than direct functional studies.
Thank you for reading.

glossary.meaning: A gene change that reduces how much the gene works.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
A way to track symptoms, daily function, or other changes in a study.
A doctor who interprets genetic test results and how they may affect health.
A cell or animal system used in research to study a condition.
A gene change where the altered gene product interferes with the normal one.
